title: Job 41
paragraphs: ¹ "Can you pull in Leviathan with a fishhook, or tie down its tongue with a rope? ² Can you put a cord through its nose, or pierce its jaw with a hook? ³ Will it keep begging you for mercy? Will it speak gentle words to you? ⁴ Will it make a covenant with you to become your servant for life? ⁵ Can you make it a pet like a bird, or put it on a leash for your girls?

⁶ Will a band of merchants try to buy it? Will they divide it up among the traders? ⁷ Can you fill its hide with harpoons, or its head with fishing spears? ⁸ Lay your hand on it — you will remember the battle and never do it again! ⁹ Look — the hope of attacking it is futile; even the sight of it is overwhelming.

¹¹ Who dares oppose me and come out alive? Everything under heaven is mine. ¹² I will not fail to speak of Leviathan's limbs, its strength, and its graceful proportions. ¹³ Who can strip off its outer coat? Who can penetrate its double coat of armor? ¹⁴ Who can open the doors of its mouth, ringed with fearsome teeth? ¹⁵ Its back has rows of shields locked tightly together as with a seal.

¹⁶ Each is so close to the next that no air can pass between them. ¹⁷ They are joined to one another; they lock together and cannot be pulled apart. ¹⁸ Its snorting flashes with light; its eyes are like the glimmer of dawn. ¹⁹ Flames stream from its mouth; sparks of fire shoot out. ²⁰ Smoke pours from its nostrils as from a boiling pot heated over rushes.

²¹ Its breath sets coals ablaze; flames dart from its mouth. ²² Strength lodges in its neck; dismay goes before it. ²³ The folds of its flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable. ²⁴ Its chest is hard as rock, hard as a lower millstone. ²⁵ When it rises up, the mighty are terrified; they fall back before its thrashing.

²⁶ The sword that strikes it cannot hold; nor can spear, dart, or javelin. ²⁷ Iron it treats like straw and bronze like rotten wood. ²⁸ Arrows do not make it flee; slingstones are like chaff to it. ²⁹ A club seems to it a piece of straw; it laughs at the rattling of the lance. ³⁰ Its underside is jagged shards; it moves across the mud like a threshing sledge.

³¹ It makes the depths churn like a boiling cauldron; it stirs up the sea like a pot of ointment. ³² It leaves a glistening wake behind it; one would think the deep had turned white. ³³ Nothing on earth is its equal — a creature without fear. ³⁴ It looks down on all that are haughty; it is king over all that are proud."
